threads.title: Caught up to the seventh heaven
threads.summary_md: Isaiah is borne to the topmost heaven and a voice asks how flesh can climb so high: *AND he took me into the air of the seventh heaven, and moreover I heard a voice saying: "How far will he ascend that dwelleth in the flesh?" And I feared and trembled.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:1) — *And he raised me up into the seventh heaven, and I saw there a wonderful light and angels innumerable.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:6). It ain't new: Paul too was *caught up to the third heaven* — *I knew a man in Messiah (Christ) above fourteen years ago, (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: Elohim (God) knoweth;) such an one caught up to the third heaven.* (2 Corinthians 12:2). John is summoned through the same opened door: *After this I looked, and, behold, a door was opened in heaven: and the first voice which I heard was as it were of a trumpet talking with me; which said, Come up hither, and I will shew thee things which must be hereafter.* (Revelation 4:1). And the light innumerable with angels is the throne-host of the Lamb: *And I beheld, and I heard the voice of many angels round about the throne and the beasts and the elders: and the number of them was ten thousand times ten thousand, and thousands of thousands;* (Revelation 5:11).

members.note: 2 Corinthians 12:2 — *I knew a man in Messiah (Christ) above fourteen years ago, (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: Elohim (God) knoweth;) such an one caught up to the third heaven.* Paul's own rapture through the heavens, body or no, matches the seer's fear at being carried up where flesh can scarcely ascend in Ascension of Isaiah 9:1.

Revelation 4:1 — *After this I looked, and, behold, a door was opened in heaven: and the first voice which I heard was as it were of a trumpet talking with me; which said, Come up hither, and I will shew thee things which must be hereafter.* John is summoned upward by a voice just as Isaiah is permitted and raised into the seventh heaven in Ascension of Isaiah 9:6.

Revelation 5:11 — *And I beheld, and I heard the voice of many angels round about the throne and the beasts and the elders: and the number of them was ten thousand times ten thousand, and thousands of thousands;* the wonderful light and angels innumerable Isaiah saw are this same uncountable throne-host in Ascension of Isaiah 9:6.

threads.title: The Beloved descends in the form of men
threads.summary_md: The angel foretells that the saints' thrones and crowns wait upon the descent of the Beloved into the world in the likeness of flesh: *And he said unto me: "Crowns and thrones of glory they do not receive, till the Beloved will descend in the form in which you will see Him descend will descend, I say into the world in the last days Yahuah (Lord), who will be called Messiah (Christ).* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:12) — *Nevertheless they see and know whose will be thrones, and whose the crowns when He has descended and been made in your form, and they will think that He is flesh and is a man.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:13). It ain't new: this is the kenosis hymn centuries early — *Who, being in the form of Elohim (God), thought it not robbery to be equal with Elohim (God):* (Philippians 2:6); *But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men:* (Philippians 2:7). The Word descended into flesh — *And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.* (John 1:14) — the One who came down from above: *And no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of Adam which is in heaven.* (John 3:13).

members.note: Philippians 2:6 — *Who, being in the form of Elohim (God), thought it not robbery to be equal with Elohim (God):* the Beloved who descends, being Yahuah and called Messiah, is the One already equal with Elohim before He stoops in Ascension of Isaiah 9:12.

Philippians 2:7 — *But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men:* the descent "in the form in which you will see Him descend" is precisely this taking of the form and likeness of men in Ascension of Isaiah 9:12.

John 1:14 — *And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.* the heavens' thought that "He is flesh and is a man" is the very Word-made-flesh whose hidden glory John beheld in Ascension of Isaiah 9:13.

John 3:13 — *And no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of Adam which is in heaven.* the Beloved made in human form is the Son of Adam who first came down from heaven in Ascension of Isaiah 9:13.

threads.title: Crucified by the god of that world, unrecognized
threads.summary_md: The vision foresees the crucifixion at the hand of the world's god, who slays the Son not knowing who He is: *And the god of that world will stretch forth his hand against the Son, and they will crucify Him on a tree, and will slay Him not knowing who He is.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:14) — *And thus His descent, as you will see, will be hidden even from the heavens, so that it will not be known who He is.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:15). It ain't new: He humbled Himself to the cross — *And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.* (Philippians 2:8) — and the just died for the unjust — *For Messiah (Christ) also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to Elohim (God), being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit:* (1 Peter 3:18). His hidden descent is the mystery of godliness *manifest in the flesh* — *And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: Elohim (God) was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory.* (1 Timothy 3:16).

members.note: Philippians 2:8 — *And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.* the Son crucified on a tree by the god of that world is the One who humbles Himself to the death of the cross in Ascension of Isaiah 9:14.

1 Peter 3:18 — *For Messiah (Christ) also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to Elohim (God), being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit:* the slaying of the Son "put to death in the flesh" yet quickened answers the cross of Ascension of Isaiah 9:14.

1 Timothy 3:16 — *And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: Elohim (God) was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory.* the descent "hidden even from the heavens" is this great mystery of Elohim manifest in flesh in Ascension of Isaiah 9:15.

threads.title: He plunders death, rises the third day, ascends
threads.summary_md: After spoiling death the Beloved rises on the third day and ascends, and the righteous rise with Him: *And when He hath plundered the angel of death, He will ascend on the third day, and he will remain in that world five hundred and forty-five days.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:16) — *And then many of the righteous will ascend with Him, whose spirits do not receive their garments till Yahuah (Lord) Messiah (Christ) ascend and they ascend with Him.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:17). It ain't new: He descended and ascended to fill all things — *(Now that he ascended, what is it but that he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth?* (Ephesians 4:9); *He that descended is the same also that ascended up far above all heavens, that he might fill all things.)* (Ephesians 4:10) — having been exalted above every name — *Wherefore Elohim (God) also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name:* (Philippians 2:9). And the heroes of faith awaited this same rising-with-Him — *Women received their dead raised to life again: and others were tortured, not accepting deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection:* (Hebrews 11:35).

members.note: Ephesians 4:9 — *(Now that he ascended, what is it but that he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth?* the plundering of the angel of death before the third-day ascent is His descent into the lower parts before rising in Ascension of Isaiah 9:16.

Ephesians 4:10 — *He that descended is the same also that ascended up far above all heavens, that he might fill all things.)* the One who rises and ascends through the heavens in Ascension of Isaiah 9:16 is the same who ascends far above all heavens to fill all things.

Philippians 2:9 — *Wherefore Elohim (God) also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name:* the third-day ascent of Ascension of Isaiah 9:16 is the exaltation that follows the humbling of the cross.

Hebrews 11:35 — *Women received their dead raised to life again: and others were tortured, not accepting deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection:* the righteous who do not receive their garments till they ascend with the Beloved await this same better resurrection in Ascension of Isaiah 9:17.

threads.title: Named in the world, believed on, His cross laid up for them
threads.summary_md: The garments are laid up for those who believe the words of That One and believe in His cross: *And he said unto me: "These garments many from that world will receive, believing in the words of That One, who shall be named as I told thee, and they will observe those things, and believe in them, and believe in His cross: for them are these laid up."* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:26). Earlier the angel named Him born into the world: *And He who permitted thee, this is thy Yahuah Elohim (LORD God), Yahuah (Lord) Messiah (Christ), who will be called 'Jesus' in the world, but His name thou canst not hear till thou hast ascended out of thy body.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:5). It ain't new: the sign of the virgin who bears the named Son — *Therefore Yahuah (Lord) himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.* (Isaiah 7:14); *Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, Elohim (God) with us.* (Matthew 1:23). And believing on His name makes sons of Elohim — *But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of Elohim (God), even to them that believe on his name:* (John 1:12).

members.note: Isaiah 7:14 — *Therefore Yahuah (Lord) himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.* the One named in the world whom Isaiah is shown is the very Immanuel-sign the prophet himself was given in Ascension of Isaiah 9:5.

Matthew 1:23 — *Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, Elohim (God) with us.* the name to be called in the world is fulfilled in Emmanuel, Elohim with us, in Ascension of Isaiah 9:5.

John 1:12 — *But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of Elohim (God), even to them that believe on his name:* those who believe the words of That One and believe in His cross, for whom the garments are laid up, are these who believe on His name in Ascension of Isaiah 9:26.

threads.title: The Beloved worshipped with the Angel of the Spirit
threads.summary_md: Isaiah sees the Glorious One adored by Adam, Abel, Seth, all the righteous and angels, then the second Glorious One, the Angel of the Spirit, worshipped beside Him before the Great Glory: *And after I had seen Him, all the righteous whom I had seen and also the angels whom I had seen came to Him. And Adam and Abel and Seth and all the righteous first drew near and worshipped Him, and they all praised Him with one voice, and I myself also gave praise with them, and my giving of praise was as theirs.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:28) — *And the second whom I saw was on the left of my Lord. And I asked: "Who is this?" and he said unto me: "Worship Him, for He is the angel of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), who speaketh in thee and the rest of the righteous."* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:36). It ain't new: the firstbegotten brought in to the worship of all the angels — *And again, when he bringeth in the firstbegotten into the world, he saith, And let all the angels of Elohim (God) worship him.* (Hebrews 1:6) — the brightness of the glory at the right hand — *Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;* (Hebrews 1:3) — until every tongue confesses Him Lord — *And that every tongue should confess that Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) is Lord, to the glory of Elohim (God) the Father.* (Philippians 2:11).

members.note: Hebrews 1:6 — *And again, when he bringeth in the firstbegotten into the world, he saith, And let all the angels of Elohim (God) worship him.* the righteous and angels worshipping the Glorious One with one voice fulfil the decree that all angels worship the firstbegotten in Ascension of Isaiah 9:28.

Hebrews 1:3 — *Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;* the One whose glory surpassed all is this brightness of the Father's glory seated at the right hand in Ascension of Isaiah 9:27.

Philippians 2:11 — *And that every tongue should confess that Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) is Lord, to the glory of Elohim (God) the Father.* the command "Worship this One" and Isaiah's praise answer the confession that every tongue gives Him as Lord in Ascension of Isaiah 9:31.
